newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba deploys anti-aircraft units on Havana seafront.
newsitem.headline: Cuba deploys anti-aircraft units on Havana seafront.

text.p: Cuba's armed forces on Tuesday deployed anti-aircraft units facing northward along Havana's seafront, apparently as part of a nationwide military drill.

One of the mobile units was positioned alongside the capital's Malecon seafront promenade, close to the Cuban Foreign Ministry. Another was placed at the mouth of the Almendares River, while a third was deployed in front of two tourist hotels, the Triton and the Neptuno, in western Havana.

The units were ZSU-23-4 Shilkas, Soviet-made tracked anti-aircraft vehicles that carries four 23mm cannon. They were apparently deployed as part of nationwide military manoeuvres announced last Saturday.

A note from the Armed Forces Ministry had warned citizens that they might see movements of troops and aircraft and hear shots and explosions. The drill would involve Cuba's Air Force and anti-aircraft defences, the April 26 note said.
Officers stationed with the anti-aircraft units declined to discuss their mission.

The manoeuvres took place two days before President Fidel Castro was to lead the nation in celebration of May 1 Workers' Day, one of the high points of the communist-ruled island's political calendar. A mass march was to be held in Havana.
